ai.literal: Without equity, if one covets the good wealth of others, their family perishing, guilt also then and there it will bring.
ai.translation: If a person, abandoning equity, covets the valuable wealth of others, it will ruin their family and bring instant guilt upon them.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமை இல்லாமல், பிறருடைய நல்ல பொருளைக் கவர விரும்பினால், அவனுடைய குடும்பம் அழிந்து, அவனுக்குப் பழியும் உடனே வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive consequences of covetousness. When a person acts without fairness (நடுவின்றி) and desires the rightfully earned, valuable wealth of another (நன்பொருள்), they bring ruin upon themselves. The poet states that such greed leads to two immediate disasters: the destruction of one's own family lineage (குடிபொன்றி) and the instant acquisition of guilt and blame (குற்றமும் ஆங்கே தரும்). Thus, coveting others' property destroys both one's social standing and moral character.

words.gloss: those who shrink in shame from

ai.literal: Those who shrink in shame from lack of equity will not do disgraceful deeds, coveting the accruing benefit.
ai.translation: Those who shrink in shame from unfairness will not commit disgraceful deeds, even for the sake of gaining some benefit.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமை இல்லாத தன்மையைக் கண்டு வெட்கப்படுபவர்கள், தமக்குக் கிடைக்கும் பயனை விரும்பிப் பழி தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the integrity of those who value justice. People who feel a deep sense of shame at the very thought of being unfair or inequitable (natuvanmai nanupavar) will never commit disgraceful acts (palippatuva ceyyar). Even when they desire the potential gains or benefits (patupayan vehki) that could arise from an action, their moral conscience prevents them from choosing a path of dishonor.

ai.literal: Petty pleasure having coveted, unrighteous deeds they will indeed not do, the other pleasure those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire the supreme, lasting bliss of virtue will not commit unrighteous deeds out of a desire for the petty, fleeting pleasure of coveting others' wealth.
ai.modern: நிலையான உயர்ந்த இன்பத்தை விரும்புபவர்கள், பிறர் பொருளைக் கவர நினைக்கும் சிற்றின்பத்தை விரும்பி அறமற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யமாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two kinds of happiness: 'சிற்றின்பம்' (the petty, transient pleasure of coveting and taking what belongs to others) and 'மற்று இன்பம்' (the other, supreme and lasting bliss that comes from a life of virtue). Those who truly seek the higher, enduring happiness will never stoop to unrighteous acts. They understand that the small gain from covetousness is fleeting and ultimately destructive to their character.

ai.literal: "We are poor," saying, coveting they will not do, the senses conquered, meanness-without vision having they.
ai.translation: Those who have conquered their senses and possess a vision free from meanness will not covet others' wealth, even when thinking, "We are destitute."
ai.modern: "நாம் வறியவர்" என்று நினைத்து, பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பும் செயலைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள், ஐம்புலன்களையும் வென்ற குற்றமற்ற அறிவுடையவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that people of pure, flawless wisdom who have mastered their five senses will never resort to coveting others' property, even in times of extreme poverty. The word 'புலம்' refers to the five senses, and 'வென்ற' means conquered, indicating self-control. 'புன்மை இல் காட்சி' refers to a perception or vision that is free from the blemish of ignorance or meanness. Such individuals do not let temporary material deprivation ('இலம்') compromise their integrity.

ai.literal: Having become subtle and widened knowledge, what use will it be, if, coveting towards anyone, one does senseless deeds?
ai.translation: Of what use is a sharp and wide-ranging wisdom if one covets others' property and commits senseless deeds against anyone?
ai.modern: நுண்ணியதாய் விரிந்த அறிவு இருந்து என்ன பயன், ஒருவன் யாரிடத்தும் பேராசை கொண்டு அறிவற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்தால்?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that intellectual development is meaningless without moral restraint. The phrase 'அஃகி அகன்ற அறிவு' describes a mind that is both sharp in its analysis and broad in its scope of knowledge. However, if a person allows greed ('வெஃகி') to take over and performs senseless or unjust deeds ('வெறிய செயின்') against anyone, that vast wisdom is rendered useless. True wisdom must guide a person to overcome covetousness and act with integrity.

ai.literal: Desiring grace, he who stood in the path, if he desires wealth and schemes evil, will perish.
ai.translation: He who stands in the path of virtue, desiring grace, will be ruined if he covets another's wealth and schemes evil deeds.
ai.modern: அருளை விரும்பி அறவழியில் நிற்பவன், பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பித் தீயவற்றை எண்ணினால் கெட்டுப்போவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive nature of covetousness. A person who has committed themselves to a life of virtue and grace (அருள்) must maintain consistency in their thoughts. If such a person, driven by greed, covets another's property (பொருள்) and begins to plot evil schemes (பொல்லாத சூழ) to acquire it, they will lose their moral standing and be completely ruined (கெடும்). The contrast between desiring grace (அருள்வெஃகி) and desiring material wealth (பொருள்வெஃகி) shows that spiritual progress is instantly destroyed by the rise of greed.

words.gloss: at the time of yielding results

ai.literal: Do not desire coveting-obtained wealth; at the time of yielding results, for being excellent rare will be the fruit.
ai.translation: Do not desire the wealth acquired by coveting others' goods; for when it yields its final results, its fruit will be devoid of any goodness.
ai.modern: பிறர் பொருளைக் கவர்ந்து பெறும் செல்வத்தை விரும்பாதீர்; அது தன் பயனைத் தரும் போது, அதன் விளைவு நன்மையாக இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against seeking wealth through covetousness. The phrase 'வெஃகி ஆம் ஆக்கம்' refers to wealth acquired by desiring and taking what belongs to others. Although such wealth might seem beneficial at first, the poet warns that 'விளைவயின்' (at the time of yielding its ultimate consequences), the actual benefit or 'பயன்' will be 'மாண்டற்கு அரிது' (extremely rare to have any goodness or dignity). In short, ill-gotten gains bring only ruin and misery in the end.

ai.literal: If asked what is the non-diminishing of wealth, it is requiring the non-coveting of the property in another's hand.
ai.translation: If you ask how to prevent your own wealth from diminishing, the answer is: you must not covet the property that belongs to another.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுடைய செல்வம் குறையாமல் இருப்பதற்கான வழி யாது என்றால், அவன் பிறனுடைய கையில் உள்ள பொருளை விரும்பாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the secret to preserving one's own wealth. The author states that if a person wishes for their wealth not to decrease (அஃகாமை), the key is to avoid coveting (வெஃகாமை) the possessions of others (பிறன்கைப்பொருள்). Covetousness leads to ruin and loss of what one already has, whereas contentment and respecting others' property secure one's own prosperity. The wordplay between 'அஃகாமை' (non-diminishing) and 'வெஃகாமை' (non-coveting) beautifully links the action of restraint to the result of preservation.

ai.literal: Knowing righteousness, those who do not covet and possess wisdom—knowing the proper way, right there, wealth will reach them.
ai.translation: Wealth, knowing the proper way, will go and reach those wise people who, knowing what is righteous, do not covet others' property.
ai.modern: அறத்தை அறிந்து பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பாத அறிவுடையவர்களிடம், செல்வம் தானே வழியறிந்து சென்று சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the natural attraction of wealth towards virtuous individuals. Those who possess wisdom understand what is righteous and refrain from coveting others' possessions. To such people, wealth itself will find its way and reach them immediately. The poet personifies wealth as an intelligent entity that actively seeks out and resides with those who practice non-covetousness.

ai.literal: Ruin will yield, without thinking if one covets; victory will yield, non-desiring which is called sublime pride.
ai.translation: Coveting another's wealth without considering the consequences brings ruin; but the sublime pride of not desiring anything brings victory.
ai.modern: விளைவுகளை ஆராயாமல் பிறர் பொருளை விரும்பினால் அது அழிவைத் தரும்; வேண்டாமை எனப்படும் பெருமித உணர்வு வெற்றியைக் கொடுக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the destructive nature of greed with the triumphant power of contentment. If a person blindly covets another's property without thinking of the moral and practical consequences, it will lead to their utter ruin (iṟal). Conversely, cultivating the state of mind that does not desire others' possessions—described here as a sublime pride or loftiness of spirit (cerukku)—brings ultimate victory and greatness (viṟal). The word 'cerukku' usually means pride, but here it beautifully denotes the noble, self-satisfied dignity of a mind that is above greed.
